podcast.body: Released on April 7, 1992, this was the first single from their comeback album, *Check Your Head*. The track was "built around a guitar sample from a bad brain song called Big Takeover" and featured a distinctive "big drum sound" achieved by using "a big 10-foot tunnel in front of the bass drum and then miking it at the end of that long barrel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The first single released from the album "Check Your Head" on April 7, 1992. It was one of the earlier rap tracks from the album, built around a guitar sample from Bad Brains' "Big Takeover" and potentially a Dr. Dre sample. The distinctive drum sound was achieved by placing a 10-foot tunnel in front of the bass drum. "That's past the mic, which was the first single released on April 7, 1992."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The song "Pass the Mic" from the Beastie Boys' 1992 album *Check Your Head* features an intricate tapestry of samples. It incorporates a flute from James Newton's 1982 track "Choir," elements from Bad Brains' "Big Takeover," a segment from EPMD's 1989 song "So What You Sayin'," a snippet from comedian Jimmy Walker's 1975 album *The Black Prince has arrived*, a bass groove from Johnny Hammond's 1974 "Big Sir Suite," a squawk from a 1969 live Jimi Hendrix recording, and a sample from Johnny Jenkins' 1970 track "I Walk on Gilded Splinters." "The songs pass the mic. Where the drum sounds come from is anybody's guess. But we can find samples of seven songs buried within this track."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
